project.name: haproxy
project.commit_note: The staged vulnerable checkout under `gt_results/arvo_417113588/_work/src/haproxy` is newer than the metadata vulnerable commit, but the traced sites still have the exact pre-fix behavior from `patch.diff`: `parse_cfg()` declares `const char *errptr;` without initialization and the empty-argument warning path still lacks the later `if (!errptr) errptr = args[check_arg] - outline + line;` fallback. This GT is grounded on that staged source.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 417113588 (haproxy): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_cfg_parser [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/417113588
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / saved sanitizer_trace.txt / exact staged vulnerable source / staged patch.diff
bug_description.normalized: The staged 118-byte `fuzz_cfg_parser` witness is passed to `parse_cfg()` as an in-memory configuration file. On the successful tokenization pass, `parse_line()` reaches the witness's final four-byte token `\x00`, decodes the hexadecimal escape under `PARSE_OPT_BKSLASH`, and emits a literal zero byte as the first byte of a fresh output argument. Because that argument both begins with NUL and ends immediately, `parse_line()` keeps `args[arg]` pointing at an empty string but never records `empty_arg_ptr`, so the convenience write-back `*errptr = empty_arg_ptr` does not run. In the vulnerable `parse_cfg()`, the local `const char *errptr;` was never initialized and the empty-argument warning block still assumes `errptr` names the offending source position, so it evaluates `sanitize_for_printing(line, errptr - line, 80)` and later formats `(errptr - thisline + 1)`. The bogus pointer difference makes `sanitize_for_printing()` take its `pos >= width` shift path, move `in` to a wild address above the real line buffer, and crash on the read `*in` at line 6600. The fix initializes `errptr = NULL` and, for rare empty-argument cases such as `\x00`, falls back to `args[check_arg] - outline + line` before calling `sanitize_for_printing()`.

source.description: Backslash-escape decoding turns the witness's final literal token `\x00` into the byte value 0, creating the attacker-controlled value that later makes the last parsed argument appear empty.
source.value_from: The exact staged 118-byte `poc` ends with bytes `5c 78 30 30` (`\\x00`). On the reproduced path `parse_cfg()` calls `parse_line()` with `PARSE_OPT_BKSLASH`, so that final token reaches the `'x'` escape branch and is decoded as hexadecimal `00`.
source.note: Source. This is the first project-side statement that consumes the witness's terminal `\x00` text and materializes the zero byte used by the empty-argument path.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After `sanitize_for_printing()` shifts `in` using the bogus `pos` derived from stale `errptr`, the loop condition dereferences one byte through that wild address.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `SEGV on unknown address` caused by a read at `src/tools.c:6600:22` in `sanitize_for_printing`, matching this `*in` dereference.

root_cause.description: The empty-argument warning path uses `errptr` as if `parse_line()` always supplied a source pointer for empty arguments. For the reproduced `\x00` case it did not, and the vulnerable code neither initialized `errptr` nor repaired it before subtracting it from `line`.
root_cause.note: The fix addresses this exact obligation by initializing `errptr = NULL` and, inside the empty-argument block, falling back to `args[check_arg] - outline + line` when `parse_line()` left `errptr` unset.

tainted_value_origin.description: The decoded zero byte is written into the parsed output buffer as the first byte of the final argument.
tainted_value_origin.note: Because `tosend == 0` for the witness's terminal `\x00` token, this emitted byte makes the new argument look empty to the later `!*args[check_arg]` test.

parser_admitted.code: err = parse_line(line, outline, &outlen, args, &arg, PARSE_OPT_ENV | PARSE_OPT_DQUOTE | PARSE_OPT_SQUOTE | PARSE_OPT_BKSLASH | PARSE_OPT_SHARP | PARSE_OPT_WORD_EXPAND, &errptr);
parser_admitted.description: After `fgets_from_mem()` copied the witness into `thisline` and leading whitespace was skipped, `parse_cfg()` entered the line tokenizer with backslash escape handling enabled, so the trailing literal `\x00` token could reach the empty-argument diagnostic path.

evidence_limitations: The staged vulnerable checkout is commit `3bb6eea6d56d0328437ed34ac97d4479051ee2c9`, newer than metadata commit `3fdb039a99cdee543f4bbbfc983a51eb18f7f1f0`. The GT relies on the exact staged source because the traced lines still match `patch.diff`'s pre-fix behavior.

Stage 01 provides the ASan stack but not the incidental garbage pointer value held in `errptr`. The trace is therefore grounded on the source fact that `parse_line()` leaves `errptr` untouched on this `\x00` path, not on any specific observed pointer value.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness wraps the exact staged `poc` as `cfgfile.content` and calls `parse_cfg()` because the witness is 118 bytes long, above the fuzzer's 50-byte size gate.
While tokenizing the attacker-controlled line, `parse_cfg()` passes the address of an uninitialized local `errptr` into `parse_line()` for later diagnostics.

The final literal token `\x00` is decoded into a NUL-only argument. `args[arg]` points at that empty string, but EOF bookkeeping never sets `empty_arg_ptr`, so `parse_line()` returns success without writing back `errptr`.
The returned empty `args[]` slot selects the empty-argument warning path, which still calls `sanitize_for_printing(line, errptr - line, 80)` without the fallback later added by the fix.
The huge bogus `pos` triggers the shift branch, moves `in` off the real line buffer, and the next loop condition crashes on `*in`.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact 118-byte witness from `poc` is wrapped as in-memory config content and passed to `parse_cfg()` because it exceeds the 50-byte size guard.

On the parse pass that reaches the warning logic, `parse_cfg()` tokenizes the copied config line with backslash escaping enabled and passes the address of a local `errptr` that has no initializer in the vulnerable source.
The witness's final token is the literal text `\x00`. In the `'x'` escape branch, `parse_line()` decodes its hexadecimal payload `00` into the byte value 0.
With `tosend == 0`, the parser writes a NUL byte into the output word buffer as the first byte of the final argument.
Because the NUL from step 4 started a fresh argument, `args[arg]` is set to the buffer position whose first byte is already `\0`. The final parsed word now aliases an empty string.

At end of input, `arg_start` has already advanced past the NUL emitted at step 4, so `args[arg] == out + arg_start` is false. The parser therefore does not record `begin_new_arg` as `empty_arg_ptr` for this NUL-only final argument.

Because step 6 left `empty_arg_ptr` NULL, this convenience write-back does not run. `parse_line()` still returns success, so `args[arg]` remains the empty string from step 5 while caller `errptr` stays untouched.
Back in `parse_cfg()`, the returned NUL-first slot satisfies `!*args[check_arg]`, so the parser selects the empty-argument warning path.

Root cause. The empty-argument warning path assumes `errptr` points into the original line and subtracts it from `line` without first checking whether `parse_line()` ever set it. On this path `errptr` is still the untouched local from step 2, so the computed `pos` is indeterminate.
The bogus `pos` from step 9 is large enough to satisfy `pos >= width`, so `sanitize_for_printing()` shifts `in` far above the real line buffer before any byte is read.
Sink. The loop condition dereferences `*in` from the shifted wild address set up in step 10, producing the saved AddressSanitizer `SEGV on unknown address` read in `sanitize_for_printing`.

cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Control-only: the decoded NUL byte does not become the crash address, but it makes the final argument empty and forces the warning path that dereferences stale `errptr`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01 reproduced the crash with the exact staged 118-byte `poc` (SHA-256 `e4a5fd78ae22b0d95684f380313044118e9ff1511f6bd4361f4617ea1cb495a1`). The harness passes it verbatim as `cfgfile.content`; its last four bytes are the literal text `5c 78 30 30` (`\\x00`), so `parse_line()` decodes the final token to a NUL-only argument and `parse_cfg()` reaches the empty-argument warning that crashes in `sanitize_for_printing()`.

format.name: haproxy-fuzz_cfg_parser
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 118-byte witness in `poc` (SHA-256 `e4a5fd78ae22b0d95684f380313044118e9ff1511f6bd4361f4617ea1cb495a1`). It is passed directly to `parse_cfg()` as one in-memory config blob, and the last four bytes must remain the literal text `\\x00` so the successful `parse_line()` pass emits a NUL-only final argument under `PARSE_OPT_BKSLASH`. That empty final argument makes `!*args[check_arg]` true while leaving `errptr` unset. This GT does not generalize beyond that exact witness and terminal `\x00` decoding behavior.
